aspects.says: A collection acts on whatever its comparator answers: reversed() on a chain reverses every key (unit 4.1.3) and a 0 from a TreeSet's comparator means duplicate (unit 1.4.4).
basis: section:The JDK's Comparator Is a Strategy, and the Sort Trusts Its Contract

aspects.says: A comparator that subtracts, or casts a long difference to int, overflows for values far apart, and List.sort then returns a wrong order or throws 'Comparison method violates its general contract!' depending on the input; Long.compare and comparingLong don't overflow.
basis: section:The JDK's Comparator Is a Strategy, and the Sort Trusts Its Contract

aspects.says: A default belongs to a config key that is absent, never to a value that is wrong.
basis: section:Resolve a Strategy's Name When the Service Starts, Not When It First Runs

aspects.says: An enum strategy is closed to other modules, can't take parameters per use, and each constant is one object for the whole JVM, so a policy with settings is a record, a class or a capturing lambda.
basis: section:A Lambda Strategy Has No Name; an Enum Strategy Has One, and One Instance per JVM

aspects.says: Enum valueOf with an unknown name throws IllegalArgumentException at start-up, with a message that lists none of the valid names.
basis: section:Resolve a Strategy's Name When the Service Starts, Not When It First Runs
aspects.reason: the wording of a JDK exception message is a detail to read, not a decision a reader makes; the alert-channel practice checks the start-up failure itself

aspects.says: A lambda strategy's toString() is a generated class name, so logs can't say which strategy ran, and mapping a config string to a lambda needs a table you write; an enum constant prints its name and valueOf reads it from config.
basis: section:A Lambda Strategy Has No Name; an Enum Strategy Has One, and One Instance per JVM

aspects.says: A strategy named in config is resolved when the service starts, and an unknown name makes start-up fail; a lookup at first use fails after the deploy, and a fallback for an unknown name never fails.
basis: section:Resolve a Strategy's Name When the Service Starts, Not When It First Runs

aspects.says: When the set of policies is fixed and the operations on them grow, a sealed type with a switch per operation (unit 8.1.2) is the alternative to a strategy interface.
basis: section:A Lambda Strategy Has No Name; an Enum Strategy Has One, and One Instance per JVM
aspects.reason: one clause pointing to unit 8.1.2, whose practices check the sealed layout

aspects.says: One strategy instance serves every thread, so fields that carry per-call values between its steps mix concurrent calls; keeping those values in locals or a value the call owns fixes it.
basis: section:A Strategy Object Is Shared, So a Field in It Is Shared State

aspects.says: Making the shared fields volatile doesn't stop the race and made it far more frequent; synchronized makes it correct but makes every caller queue behind one lock, including behind a slow call.
basis: section:A Strategy Object Is Shared, So a Field in It Is Shared State
